q-68888.name: Question 1
q-68888.problem: Jordan did an experiment in his Chemistry class. He heated a liquid whose initial temperature was $-{1.2}^{∘}\,\text{C}.$ After several minutes, the temperature of the liquid increased by ${7.3}^{∘}\,\text{C}$, at which point he decided to end the experiment. What was the final temperature of the liquid?
q-68888.worked_solution:
To determine the final temperature of the liquid, we add the variation in temperature to the initial temperature of the liquid. This gives

$$
-{1.2}^{∘}\,\text{C}+{7.3}^{∘}\,\text{C}={6.1}^{∘}\,\text{C}.
$$

Therefore, the temperature of the liquid at the end of the experiment was ${6.1}^{∘}\,\text{C}.$

Question 1
?

Jordan did an experiment in his Chemistry class. He heated a liquid whose initial temperature was −1.2∘C. After several minutes, the temperature of the liquid increased by 7.3∘C, at which point he decided to end the experiment. What was the final temperature of the liquid?

a
5.1∘C
b
6.1∘C
c
5.5∘C
d
5.7∘C
e
6.5∘C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To determine the final temperature of the liquid, we add the variation in temperature to the initial temperature of the liquid. This gives −1.2∘C+7.3∘C=6.1∘C.

Therefore, the temperature of the liquid at the end of the experiment was 6.1∘C.

q-68925.name: Question 2
q-68925.problem: In Toronto, Canada, the average temperature in November is ${4.9}^{∘}\,\text{C}.$ In December, the average temperature decreases by ${5.4}^{∘}\,\text{C}$ compared to November. Finally, in January, the average temperature decreases by ${3.2}^{∘}\,\text{C}$ compared to the previous month. Determine the average temperature in Toronto in January.
q-68925.worked_solution:
First, we must determine the average temperature in Toronto during the month of December. Since we know that the temperature decreases on average by ${5.4}^{∘}\,\text{C}$ compared to November, we subtract the variation in temperature from the average temperature in November. This gives

$$
{4.9}^{∘}\,\text{C}-{5.4}^{∘}\,\text{C}=-{0.5}^{∘}\,\text{C}.
$$

Now, we must determine the temperature during the month of January. Since we know that the temperature decreases on average by ${3.2}^{∘}\,\text{C}$ compared to December, we subtract the variation in temperature from the average temperature in December. This gives

$$
-{0.5}^{∘}\,\text{C}-{3.2}^{∘}\,\text{C}=-{3.7}^{∘}\,\text{C}.
$$

Therefore, the average temperature in Toronto in January is $-{3.7}^{∘}\,\text{C}.$

Question 2

In Toronto, Canada, the average temperature in November is 4.9∘C. In December, the average temperature decreases by 5.4∘C compared to November. Finally, in January, the average temperature decreases by 3.2∘C compared to the previous month. Determine the average temperature in Toronto in January.

a
−2.9∘C
b
−5.5∘C
c
−3.7∘C
d
−5.3∘C
e
−3.4∘C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we must determine the average temperature in Toronto during the month of December. Since we know that the temperature decreases on average by 5.4∘C compared to November, we subtract the variation in temperature from the average temperature in November. This gives 4.9∘C−5.4∘C=−0.5∘C.

Now, we must determine the temperature during the month of January. Since we know that the temperature decreases on average by 3.2∘C compared to December, we subtract the variation in temperature from the average temperature in December. This gives −0.5∘C−3.2∘C=−3.7∘C.

Therefore, the average temperature in Toronto in January is −3.7∘C.
